newsitem.title: USA: Clinton back at White House after knee surgery.
newsitem.headline: Clinton back at White House after knee surgery.

text.p: President Bill Clinton returned to the White House in a wheelchair on Sunday after nearly 48 hours in the hospital for emergency surgery to repair a knee tendon injured in a freak accident.

"I feel fine today. I was a little sore yesterday, you know, the first day after the operation when the painkillers started to wear off," the president told reporters as his wife Hillary rolled him into the Executive Mansion.

"Hillary wanted me to come home before she left for Africa. She and Chelsea wanted me well settled," he said. Mrs. Clinton and daughter Chelsea, 17, were departing on a two-week goodwill trip to sub-Saharan Africa on Sunday afternoon. They depalyed their departure by one day after Clinton's injury.

Clinton, at 50 the youngest U.S. president since John Kennedy in the early 1960s, tore a tendon in his right knee early Friday when he stumbled on a step at the Florida home of Australian golf professional Greg Norman.

The painful injury forced him to undergo surgery later the same day, and doctors say it will be weeks before he is fully mobile again. As Clinton left the hospital, the White House announced that his Helsinki summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin will start one day later than scheduled this week -- on Thursday instead of Wednesday -- to give him more time to recuperate.

A member of the medical team that operated on Clinton was expected to accompany him to the summit, along with a physical therapist and the physicans who routinely accompany a president on foreign trips.
A Clinton visit to Denmark that was to have followed the summit is being postponed until July, the White House said.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton was in a wheelchair because his doctors felt it would make him more comfortable during a 20-minute mini-van trip from Bethesda National Navy Medical Centre.
In preparation for Clinton's return to the White House, workers rearranged furniture and taped down rugs to enable him to navigate the executive mansion on crutches.

Asked if his knee hurts every time he moves, Clinton said: "No. You just have to learn to use a few different muscles. I mwan, it will be a learning experience. It's like going back to school and learning some new things."
Clinton's accident forced him to forgo a traditional St. Patrick's Day meeting on Monday with a senior Irish official. Prime Minister John Bruton will meet with Vice President Al Gore.
However, Clinton planned to go ahead with a brief meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, who is in Washington to prepare for the Helsinki summit.
